Write one chart to an HTML page, an SVG image, and a PNG image.

## Code

The chart plots weight against fuel economy for the 32 cars of R's `mtcars` data, bundled with phiz as [`resources/data/mtcars.csv`](https://github.com/phpstats/phiz/blob/main/resources/data/mtcars.csv).

## Result

The SVG file:

{{< include ../_generated/example-save-output.md >}}

`save()` picks the format from the file extension: `html` (or `htm`), `json`, `svg`, `png`, `jpg` (or `jpeg`), or `pdf`. Any other extension throws an `InvalidArgumentException`.

- **HTML is drawn by the browser.** The page holds the Vega-Lite specification and loads vega, vega-lite, and vega-embed from the jsDelivr CDN, so it needs a network connection to display. Tooltips and other interaction work there. For a page that works offline, write `$plot->html(assets: Assets::inline(...))` to a file ([HTML](../rendering.qmd#html)).
- **Images are rendered by vl-convert.** SVG, PNG, JPG, and PDF need the vl-convert binary, which renders without a browser. Without it, `save()` throws `Phiz\Exceptions\VlConvertNotFound` with installation instructions ([Installing vl-convert](../rendering.qmd#installing-vl-convert)). Images are static, so interaction is lost.
- **`scale: 2`** doubles the pixel dimensions of PNG and JPG files. It is also the default.
- **`json`** writes the Vega-Lite specification.
- **Reproducibility.** With the same vl-convert version, the same specification produces the same SVG bytes on every run, except for unseeded jitter ([Reproducible SVG](../rendering.qmd#reproducible-svg)).
